author: Traditionally Moses
authorNote: Jewish and Christian tradition names Moses. Many modern scholars think the five books of the Law were drawn together from several sources over centuries, reaching their final form around the 6th–5th century BC; others defend substantial Mosaic authorship.
date: Traditionally c. 1400s BC; final form debated (see Genesis)
overview: Leviticus gives instructions for sacrifices, priests, clean and unclean, and Israel's festivals, including the Day of Atonement. Its repeated call is "Be holy, because I am holy." It also contains the command to "love your neighbor as yourself" (19:18).
storyPlace: Israel is camped at Mount Sinai. The book explains how a holy God can live among imperfect people.
